literal_statement:
Let $D$ be the closed unit disk, let $N$ be a (usually very big) positive integer, and let $\|\cdot\|_p$ denote the $\ell^p$ norm on $\mathbb{C}^N$. Let $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_k$ be $k$ functions in $H^\infty(D,\mathbb{C}^N)$. For each fixed $z\in D$, define
$$
M(z)=\operatorname{span}\{f_1(z),f_2(z),\ldots,f_k(z)\}.
$$
Suppose that $g\in H^\infty(D,\mathbb{C}^N)$ satisfies $\|g(z)\|_p\le 1$ for all $z\in D$ and
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{\ell^p}(g(z),M(z))\le\varepsilon
$$
for almost every $z\in T$. Does it follow that
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{\ell^p}(g(0),M(0))\le\varepsilon?
$$
The report states that the answer is no, by an almost embarrassingly simple counterexample.
